technical_requirements: Throughput target: baseline 45-55 requests/sec (short-turn chat); peak spikes up to 150 req/sec for 20–40 minute windows.
Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms for 32-token replies; p95 target for long-form (512 tokens) < 800ms if routed to large context model.
Context length: need testing @16k, 32k, and 64k. Will choose depending on perf/cost tradeoff and caching effectiveness.
Model candidates: Open-v1-family (medium/large), customer-curated LLM v2 (fine-tuned on manuals). Must validate quantization profiles.
Quantization: prefer int8 where quality acceptable; trial int4 for cost-optimized reranking pipelines; require explicit quality regression tests.
Batching/KV cache: want autoscaling-friendly batching with prefix/KV cache retention across session for operator flows; target TTL ~30m per session.
Network: on-prem deployment with VPC peering, strict egress rules; expect throughput tests to be run from inside customer's subnet for realistic latency.
Reliability: automatic fallback to smaller, cheaper model variant when dedicated pool exhausted; can accept slightly higher latency during fallback.
Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency histograms, per-route tracing required for incident RCA.
SLA: 99.95% uptime target for production clusters; maintenance windows no more than 4 hours/month with advance notice.
sla_negotiation_points: Customer pushes for 99.95% uptime; Redwood proposed 99.9% with credit tiers. Legal to reconcile credit calc and maximum cap.
Maintenance window: Redwood proposed flexible maintenance with 72-hour notice; customer requests blackout windows for shift changes.
Throughput guarantees: customer wants guaranteed minimum tokens/sec during committed period; Redwood to map to reserved GPU vCPU counts and queue limits.
Penalties: customer requested financial credits tied to lost throughput during peak windows — Redwood to propose service credits + technical mitigations (burst capacity).
Data residency & KMS: explicit clause for customer-managed KMS and proof of destruction for ephemeral caches required by their compliance team.
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial recommended commit: 8x A10G-equivalent GPUs reserved per site (2 sites) to meet baseline with headroom for caching and batching.
Burst plan: additional pooled burst capacity in hosted region (non-sensitive workloads) for 3x spike coverage; charged per-minute during bursts.
Autoscaling: scale-up policy based on 95th percentile request rate over 5-minute windows; scale-down with 15-minute cool-down.
Pre-warm: schedule pre-warm before known peak windows (08:00 and 16:30 local) to avoid cold-start latency; include automated warm-up traffic script.
Capacity validation: run 2-week stress POC with synthetic traffic matching operator patterns (50% short-turn, 50% long-form) and review token/sec vs cost.
model_tuning_preferences: Context-length experiments: run controlled A/B at 16k vs 32k to capture token-cost delta and effect on response quality.
Quantization profile: baseline on fp16, then int8; carry out quality regression tests on 1k prompt set; if int4 used, restrict to reranking or batch jobs.
KV cache strategy: keep per-session KV cache for 30m by default; introduce LRU eviction for sessions >10k tokens to bound memory.
Batching heuristics: target dynamic batching up to 8 requests per micro-batch for chat; strict latency overrides for pinned low-latency flows.
Fallback policies: primary—dedicated high-capacity; secondary—hosted warm variant; tertiary—local limited-model with cached replies for critical flows.
Quality monitoring: integrate Redwood Optimize checks; define prompt set of 200 critical instructions for weekly regression alerts.
